title: Criminology, B.S. (College of the Liberal Arts)
notes: Confirmed identical to the 2022-23 edition (see CRIMBS-2022.json), verified by fetching the 2023-24 archive page directly (raw HTML, cross-checked semester subtotals against the page's own 'Total Credits 121'): same 121-credit total, same Common Requirements for the Major and same four Options with identical course lists for the Computing and Statistics option this plan models, same eight-semester course placement, and no LA 83/LA 283 seminar requirement yet (added starting with the 2025-26 edition -- see CRIMBS-2025.json / CRIMBS-2026.json). Two real, purely textual differences found on this year's own archive page versus 2022-23, neither affecting any course, credit, or sequencing requirement: (1) the University Requirements/General Education Notes section's US/IL line changed from 'used to designate courses that satisfy University Requirements (United States and International Cultures)' (2022-23 wording) to 'used to designate courses that satisfy Cultural Diversity Requirements (United States and International Cultures)' (2023-24 wording onward) -- a university-wide policy-label rename. (2) This year's archive page also explicitly publishes a second, distinct 'Criminology, B.S. at Commonwealth Campuses' Suggested Academic Plan alongside the University Park one: same 121 total credits and same course list, but CRIM 249 and CRIM 250W are both shifted to Third Year (instead of UP's Second Year Fall/Spring split) -- confirming this is the same Pattern-A shared curriculum with a different suggested pacing at Commonwealth campuses, not a different degree; the University Park sequence is what this file models, matching CRIMBS-2026.json's own convention of only modeling the University Park plan (the department's own real 'Where can I complete this program?' section for this B.S. lists only 'End Campus: University Park', so Commonwealth-campus completion here is a 2+2 feeder into the same UP degree, not a separately offered program). STAT 200's real MATH 3 -> MATH 4 -> MATH 21 prereq-chain gap and the SOC 207 -> SOC 470 gap are identical to CRIMBS-2022.json's own notes (same underlying, catalog-year-stable course-description data). Race/Ethnicity/Gender and 4XX CRIM Core/Non-Core match patterns are reused from CRIMBS-2026.json's own department-checksheet-sourced lists for the same reason given in CRIM-2022.json's notes: no bulletin edition checked publishes the list content on the program page itself. Built the same way as CRIMBS-2022.json: no LA 83/LA 283, and 'LA' dropped from departments (no LA course appears anywhere else in this plan).
